sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 6278.2 ± 44.7 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Receptor activity assay: BRIL+LgBit double-tagged construct 'only marginally affected receptor activity' (PMC10286997, S1C Fig and S1 Table). N-terminal Flag-tagged construct used for biochemical assays in mammalian cells (PMC10286997, L9).
sites.rationale: MRGPRX1 has no signal peptide (raw topology begins O at residue 1), so the N-terminus (residues 1-29) is the sole extracellular terminus; a prepend tag (insert_after_residue=0) places the insert on the extracellular face, 29 residues upstream of TM1 (residue 30), well above the >=3-residue minimum. No paper names a specific junction residue, but topology leaves exactly one extracellular terminus, so the position is topology-derived. L3 provides the strongest functional evidence: the BRIL+LgBit double-tagged full-length receptor retained activity ('only marginally affected'). L9 independently confirms N-terminal Flag tagging in mammalian cells for biochemical assays. Full-length MRGPRX1 expressed with BRIL fused at the N-terminus and LgBit at the C-terminus (PMC10286997); the N-terminus (residues 1-29) is extracellular with no signal peptide, making it the sole extracellular terminus. Multiple independent studies (PMC10286997, PMC10435460) report BRIL fused at the N-terminus of full-length membrane-anchored MRGPRX1; PMC10286997 also reports N-terminal Flag tag in mammalian pCDNA3.1 for biochemical assays (L9).

sources.claim: The fusion of BRIL and LgBit to receptor only marginally affected receptor activity ( S1C Fig and S1 Table ).

literature_notes: All ledger lines converge on two positions: the extracellular N-terminus (L3, L4, L5, L7, L8, L9) and the intracellular C-terminus (L1, L2, L6). No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 86-96, ECL2 164-177, ECL3 243-254), so no internal loop sites are proposed. L4 (pFastBac, HA signal peptide + N-terminal Flag + C-terminal 10xHis) also supports the N-terminal extracellular site but is from the same paper as L3/L5/L9 (PMC10286997); L3 is used as primary because it explicitly reports functional retention. L7 and L8 (PMC10435460) independently confirm BRIL at the N-terminus of full-length MRGPRX1 for structural studies. The C-terminal tags (L1, L2, L6) are all intracellular and are recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: mApple red fluorescent protein fused to the intracellular C-terminus; receptor internalizes upon agonist stimulation, confirming the tag is cytoplasmic.
LgBit fused to the C-terminus of MRGPRX1 as part of NanoBit tethering strategy to stabilize the MRGPRX1-Gαq complex; C-terminus (residues 276-322) is intracellular.
LgBit fused at the C-terminus of MRGPRX1 to stabilize the whole MRGPRX1-Gαq complex for structural studies; C-terminus is intracellular.
